Legal Standards.name: Endangered Species Act (ESA) Biological Opinions (BiOps)
Legal Standards.note: Provide one of the strongest legal bases for environmental flow requirements, implemented through enforceable species-specific ecological health and habitat requirements.

Legal Standards.name: California Water Code (Flow Authority)
Legal Standards.note: Does not establish direct regulatory standards for functional flows due to the absence of state or federal flow standards. Instead, it provides legal authority to address flows indirectly through existing regulatory controls.

Legal Standards.name: Regional Flow Requirements (Regulatory Instruments)
Legal Standards.note: Environmental and operational flow requirements are imposed regionally through a combination of federal and state regulatory instruments.

key_elements.instrument: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) Orders
key_elements.context: Sometimes issued in response to ESA Biological Opinions

key_elements.instrument: Clean Water Act Section 401 Water Quality Certification
key_elements.authority: Water quality-based conditions under the CWA

key_elements.note: Additional federal, state, or local regulations that may impose flow-related conditions.

Tier 1.threshold: Functional ecosystem: functional flows to sustain native freshwater species in 90% of years; higher mean daily flows in spring/winter than summer.

policies.note: Functional flows are implemented as ordered; flows are managed based on total supply. Curtailments occur only in aggregate relative to total supply, not individual rights.
Includes flow release triggers by water year type, biological monitoring, sediment transport, and water temperature compliance.
No direct curtailments triggered by ESA or hydropower legislation, SWRCB orders, or other regulations. Compliance is enforced via litigation with lag time.

Tier 2.threshold: Modified functional flows: partial functional flows in wet season and spring; full functional flows in summer in 75% of years; higher mean daily flows in spring/winter than summer.

policies.note: Flows reduced for streams; annual variation pattern maintained minimally based on available water budgets. Compliance addressed through litigation as in Tier 1.

Tier 3.threshold: Existing flow requirements: CalSim minimum flow constraints for Baseline Scenario in 50% of years.

policies.note: Flows reduced most of the year to maintain only mandated minimum flows and other minimum system requirements. Compliance addressed via litigation as in previous tiers.

Tier 4.threshold: No function: none of the above thresholds met.

policies.note: Exceptionally severe drought/scarcity; available supplies used according to priority and rights in time to meet basic health and food safety.
